subject: reducing plot area after opening tree 180 degrees

messages.author: aa76bc9ea2907e22
messages.subject: reducing plot area after opening tree 180 degrees
parts:
Hi ggtreers,

I am trying to plot two circular trees that have been "opened" 180 degrees, but one is rotated so they sit on top of each other in a full circle.
When I arrange the trees with grid.arrange, there is a huge amount of space between the plots (see attached)

code:

library(ggtree)
library(ape)
tr <- ggtree(rcoal(100)) %>% open_tree(180)
tr2 <- tr %>% rotate_tree(180)
grid.arrange(tr,tr2,ncol = 1)

Using theme(plot.margin = unit(c(0,0-1,0,0), "cm")) on tr1 and the reverse on tr2 does not quite work - the plotting area of one cover the other. I have to edit in illustrator after to "unmask" it.
It would be great to get the end result of two mirrored trees in a circle that i can display some data on, with out having to post edit the plot in illustrator

I have tried using ylim, but it does not seem to maintain the open angle after i implement it, and i can't figure out the dimensions i should use.

Any thoughts?

Cheers in advanced

Pete
